title: Sunny and the Winter Stars | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka lies in the cold winter grass and discovers that the colder and clearer the night, the more stars come out — until the whole sky is the most crowded, brilliant thing she has ever seen. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The cold made the stars sharper.

Sunny had noticed this before but never really thought about it until tonight. On warm nights the stars were soft — still there, still beautiful, but with edges that blurred slightly into the warm air. Tonight the cold had cleared the sky completely, and every star had a point, a precision, a brightness that made it feel close.

She lay back in the frosty grass.

It crunched softly under her.

She looked up.

There were so many. More than usual. The Milky Way was there — a wide smear of white across the dark — and on either side of it, thousands of individual stars, each one a bright hard point of light. She could see stars she had never noticed before. Clusters. Pairs. A single star so bright it cast a shadow.

Her breath came out in a small cloud.

She thought: winter is cold but it gives you the best sky.

She pulled her paws in close to her chest and settled deeper into her fur.

The grass was cold below her. The stars were brilliant above her. In between, she was perfectly warm.

She found the pattern of stars she always looked for first — four of them in a rough square, like a kite.

She said hello to them.

The winter stars said nothing, but they were very bright.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, winter stars. Goodnight, little one.
